title: The Pythagorean theorem
body: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a squared plus b squared equals c squared, where c is the side opposite the right angle. The converse also holds: any triangle whose sides satisfy the relation contains a right angle. Triples of whole numbers satisfying it, such as 3, 4, 5 and 5, 12, 13, are called Pythagorean triples. The theorem fails on curved surfaces; on a sphere, the angles of a triangle sum to more than 180 degrees and the relation no longer applies.
